no_mutation_leaves_a_real_defect_passing.detail: This is the test the builder proposed and it holds, though not always through SELFCLAIM. M2, the honest removal in all three places, is correctly silent at exit 0. M3 fires with the right diagnosis: 'the module emits [NEWKIND], which the contract does not describe'. M5b and M5c each fire naming the renamed kind correctly. M4, an eighth check with no name in the tuple, raises AttributeError in kinds() and exits 1 - fail-loud rather than fail-silent, ugly but safe. M5a, renaming only the Defect literal so check_reference emits 'REF', leaves the grader at exit 0 and SELFCLAIM silent, but selfcheck exits 1 because the REFERENCE case no longer fires. Under every mutation tried, the build refuses. Last round M1 left a real VOLATILE defect passing at exit 0; it no longer does. That is a measurable improvement, not a cosmetic one.
no_mutation_leaves_a_real_defect_passing.caveat: Strictly on the builder's own wording - 'if any of those leaves a real defect of that kind passing while SELFCLAIM stays silent' - M5a is such a case. It is caught by the sibling check, not by SELFCLAIM.

the_builders_reported_M1_result_reproduc.detail: It does not. The builder reports re-running this witness's exact mutation - delete check_volatile from ALL_CHECKS, leave the contract untouched - and getting "the contract describes ['VOLATILE'], which the module does not emit". Run here, that mutation yields "the contract describes ['SELFCLAIM'], which the module does not emit". The reason is the zip: with six checks and seven names, zip truncates and every label after the deletion point shifts, so check_retired is labelled VOLATILE, check_provenance is labelled RETIRED, check_selfclaim is labelled PROVENANCE, and kinds() reports a VOLATILE that no longer runs while omitting the SELFCLAIM that does. The reported output corresponds to deleting the name from the tuple as well, which is a two-place mutation, not the one-place mutation described. The substantive conclusion the builder drew is still sound - the build does refuse - but the reported evidence is not the evidence the shipped code produces.

the_kind_set_is_now_derived_from_what_ru.detail: Partly, and materially better than the frozenset it replaces. kinds() reads check.kind off ALL_CHECKS membership, so len(kinds()) is 7 and equals len(ALL_CHECKS), the summary line is computed rather than incremented, and adding or removing a check changes the set. What is still asserted is the mapping: the kind names remain a literal tuple positionally zipped onto ALL_CHECKS, so the name is a declaration about a function rather than a measurement of what that function emits. M5a is the proof - a function can emit 'REF' while its label says 'REFERENCE' and SELFCLAIM cannot tell. The data needed to close this already exists in the CASES table, which maps a triggering fixture to an expected kind; asserting each check's emitted Defect.kind against its declared kind would make the label a measurement.

F10_is_closed.detail: check_selfclaim is a member of ALL_CHECKS, the contract's coverage.derived describes SELFCLAIM, and the build is green with it described - the structural self-exemption is gone. The kind count in the summary is len(kinds()), computed from membership, and the hardcoded +1 is removed. The contract now describes exactly the seven kinds the module runs, verified by set comparison.

the_shipped_flag_framing_is_honest.detail: Judged as asked rather than verified, and the framing is honest. Whether a defect actually reached this repository is a historical fact with no in-tree referent to derive it from, the comment says exactly that, and it explicitly names why the previous shape was worse: nothing tied a name in the separate tuple to a case, and the old comment claimed a basis - reading the why field - that no code implemented. Moving the flag onto the case it describes removes the drift surface without pretending to a derivation. Declaring a fact that cannot be derived, and saying so, is the correct move; that is not dressing up a literal.

This is not pedantry about a directory listing: _roots() enumerates services/* to build REFERENCE's resolution roots, and the set of those directories changes the verdict. judgement_asked_by_the_builder.question: Five of the ten regression cases are defects in this branch's own grader. Is that a grader converging, or a grader whose design keeps producing the same defect in new places? Withdraw SELFCLAIM if the second.
judgement_asked_by_the_builder.answer: Do not withdraw SELFCLAIM. It is converging on the mechanism and not converging on the category, and those need different remedies.
judgement_asked_by_the_builder.converging: The mutation battery is materially harder to defeat than one commit ago. Last round deleting a check left a real defect passing at exit 0; now every mutation tried refuses, the honest removal is correctly silent, and four of the five kind mutations are diagnosed correctly by SELFCLAIM itself. The footprint derivation is live rather than pinned - it caught a planted thirteenth citation. Fixtures went from nine to fifteen cases, and the two weaknesses named last round were not patched over but replaced with stronger cases whose index state verifies. Four findings closed outright. That is convergence, and SELFCLAIM is load-bearing in it.
judgement_asked_by_the_builder.not_converging: One category has now recurred three times in three commits: a hand-maintained list that must be kept in step with something the code already knows. The contract summary's kind tally, then the SHIPPED tuple, then the fixtures docstring. The observes tuple has recurred three times. The kind-name tuple is the same category again, now positionally coupled. Each repair has been local to the instance named rather than to the category, so the category keeps reappearing one layer out.
judgement_asked_by_the_builder.correction_to_the_premise: These were not found by reading rather than running. F9 was found by running a mutation, and so were the zip misalignment and the services input this round. What is true is that they were found by running the grader against trees the shipped fixtures do not build. The fixtures test the tree the grader reads; nothing tests the grader under mutation of itself. That is the missing check, and it is buildable from the CASES table already present rather than as new machinery.
judgement_asked_by_the_builder.recommendation: Stop repairing instances and put one check on the category. Bind each kind at its definition so no zip can misalign it; assert each check's emitted kind against its declared kind using the fixtures that already exist; and stop writing a population count in prose that the same file computes. Grading observes against the paths a check opens is the same category and is already named repository-wide in scripts/sovland/isolation.py, so it is larger than this concern.
